_comment: CAMERA JOURNEYS — what a session actually looks like. A SESSION IS NEVER A TELEPORT.
Every other corpus here describes a SKETCH (tools/corpus_tube.loft, match_parity) — what the router
is asked. None of them describe what the MAP is asked, and the map is where the waiting happens.
A journey is a walk: get your bearings wide, zoom in on somewhere, then work along the ground.
Each step is one camera the user comes to rest at. `why` is the human reason, and it is not
decoration: a step that cannot be explained in a phrase is a step no user takes, and a corpus of
those measures nothing. `expect` names the block that SHOULD answer, so a run reports a scale
change instead of leaving the reader to infer one from timings.
So z11 -> z13 -> z15 crosses BOTH boundaries, and each crossing is a different store, cold.

journeys.name: Bearings, then Amsterdam, then north along the coast
journeys.why: The ordinary shape of a visit: see the whole area, choose somewhere, go there, work along it.

steps.why: arrives in the city — second scale change
back out to plan the way north
Egmond aan Zee — reaches the coast
Bergen aan Zee, along the coast
Den Helder — end of the coast run

journeys.name: Small pans at one zoom — does the ring earn its bytes?
journeys.why: The ring pages 3x3 screens after every view so the next pan is a redraw. This is the corpus that says whether it works: quarter-screen nudges should be ~free, and a full screen should be the first that is not.

steps.why: a full screen east — past the ring
